chordInfo.name: Altered Dominant Chords
chordInfo.subtitle: Unlock the power of altered dominants - from the iconic Hendrix chord to jazz tension mastery, these modified dominant 7ths create maximum harmonic tension before resolution.

fundamentals.label: Definition
fundamentals.value: Dominant 7th chords with a raised or lowered 5th and/or 9th

fundamentals.label: Function
fundamentals.value: Maximum tension before resolution to tonic chord

applications.label: Rock/Blues
applications.value: The 'Hendrix chord' E7#9 - Purple Haze, Foxy Lady

applications.value: Altered dominants in ii-V-I resolutions and turnarounds

boxes.title: E7#9 (The Hendrix Chord)
items: Root: E (1st degree)
Major 3rd: G# (creates dominant quality)
Perfect 5th: B (standard 5th)
Minor 7th: D (dominant 7th tension)
Augmented 9th: G-natural (clashes with G# for gritty dissonance)

boxes.title: Altered Tensions Explained
items: #9 (sharp nine): Raised 9th - the 'Hendrix' sound
b9 (flat nine): Lowered 9th - dark, dramatic tension
#5 (sharp five): Raised 5th - augmented dominant color
b5 (flat five): Lowered 5th - tritone substitution foundation
Full alt: All alterations from the altered scale (7th mode of melodic minor)

boxes.title: The Altered Scale Connection
items: Source: 7th mode of melodic minor (Ab melodic minor gives G altered)
Contains: Root, b9, #9, 3, b5, #5, b7
Every extension is altered - no natural 5th or 9th
Provides melodic material over any altered dominant chord
Resolution: Altered V7 resolves to I with maximum voice-leading pull

items.title: Hendrix-Style E7#9 Vamp

strumming.description: Aggressive, rhythmic stabs with muted scratches

items.description: The classic Hendrix sound - sharp-nine chords with aggressive rhythm create the psychedelic blues-rock tone heard on Purple Haze and Foxy Lady.

items.title: Jazz ii-V-I with Altered V7
items.description: The cornerstone of jazz harmony - the altered dominant creates maximum tension on the V chord before resolving beautifully to the tonic major seventh.

items.title: Minor Key Altered Resolution
items.description: The flat-nine dominant is the natural V chord in harmonic minor. The b9 pulls strongly downward, creating a dark, classical-sounding resolution to the minor tonic.

items.title: Funk 7#9 Groove

strumming.description: Tight 16th-note funk pattern with ghost strums

items.description: Sharp-nine chords are a funk staple. The dissonant, biting quality of the #9 cuts through a full band mix and adds rhythmic edge to tight 16th-note grooves.

techniqueItems: Master the E7#9 shape first - thumb over the top for the low E string
Practice muting unused strings to keep altered voicings clean
Work on moving the E7#9 shape chromatically up the neck as a barre chord
Use staccato (short, clipped) attacks for funk-style altered chord stabs
applicationItems: Altered dominants create the strongest possible tension before resolution
The #9 chord works in blues, rock, funk, and jazz - an incredibly versatile sound
b9 chords naturally resolve to minor keys (V7b9 to im)
Combine altered chords with the altered scale for improvisation over changes

practiceExercises.title: Practice Exercises
practiceExercises.tipDescription: These exercises will help you internalize the sound and feel of altered dominant chords across multiple musical contexts.

exercises.title: Exercise 1: E7#9 Shape Mastery
exercises.detail: Master the moveable E7#9 barre chord shape by shifting it chromatically and to common positions up the neck
exercises.tip: Keep your thumb wrapped over the top of the neck for the bass note - this is one case where thumb fretting is standard technique

exercises.title: Exercise 2: Altered ii-V-I Resolution Drill
exercises.content: Pattern: Dm7 - G7b9 - Cmaj7, Cm7 - F7#9 - Bbmaj7, Fm7 - Bb7b9 - Ebmaj7. Transpose through all keys.
exercises.detail: Practice the most common jazz resolution using altered dominants - hear how the tension of the altered chord makes the resolution more satisfying
exercises.tip: Focus on smooth voice leading - the altered tones should resolve by half-step into chord tones of the target chord

exercises.title: Exercise 3: Funk Rhythm with Altered Chords
exercises.content: 16th-note pattern on E7#9: rest-strum-mute-strum (xU xU xU DU). Add ghost strums on muted strings between chord hits.
exercises.detail: Apply the sharp-nine chord in a tight funk rhythm context with muted ghost notes for percussive groove
exercises.tip: The key to a great funk altered-chord sound is the muting - your fretting hand should lightly release pressure between hits for crisp staccato

concepts.title: The Altered Scale (Super Locrian)
items: The altered scale is the 7th mode of melodic minor (G altered = Ab melodic minor)
Formula: 1 - b9 - #9 - 3 - b5 - #5 - b7 (every possible alteration)
Use it to solo over any altered dominant chord (7alt, 7#9, 7b9, 7#5, 7b5)
It resolves naturally - every note wants to move by half-step to a chord tone of the I chord
Also called 'Super Locrian' or 'Diminished Whole-Tone' scale

concepts.title: Tritone Substitution and Altered Chords
items: A tritone sub replaces V7 with bII7 (e.g., Db7 instead of G7 in key of C)
The altered tones of G7 (b5, #5) are the natural tones of Db7 and vice versa
G7#5 shares notes with Db7: same tritone (B-F), enharmonic extensions
This is why altered dominants sound 'outside' - they imply two keys simultaneously
Master tritone subs to unlock chromatic bass lines: Dm7 - Db7 - Cmaj7
